description: A stiff, erect, more or less evergreen dwarf shrub; stems branched, up to 80 cm high, woody at the base. Leaves oval 25–60 cm long with a strong goat-like smell on crushing. Flowers 35–40 mm across, in cymes. Stamens in 5 bundles, longer than the petals. Styles 3, much longer than the ovary.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A bushy plant up to 70 cm high; stems woody at the base. Leaves 50–100 mm, oval obtuse. Flowers 20 mm across, in small cymes. Stamens in 5 bundles, about equalling the petals. Styles 3, shorter than the ovary. Capsule fleshy, berry-like, first red, then black.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, shortly downy perennial; stems cylindrical, without raised lines, up to 100 cm high. Leaves oval-oblong, obtuse. Flowers 15–20 mm across, in cymes. Sepals fringed with stalked black glands. Petals sometimes streaked with red.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A slender plant, with erect, smooth stems 25–35 cm high. Leaves oval, obtuse, with numerous translucent glands. Petals and sepals fringed with shortly stalked black glands; petals often tinged with red on lower side.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Usually woolly (but occasionally, when submerged in a stream or pool, almost hairless). Stems creeping and rooting at the base, erect above. Leaves 10–15 mm, almost circular, clasping the stem. Flowers 15 mm across, in small cymes. Sepals fringed with red glands; petals pale yellow.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems numerous, trailing or prostrate, branched, 10–20 cm long. Leaves 10 mm × 3 mm, oblong, obtuse, with numerous translucent glands and a few black glands near the margin. Flowers few, 8–10 mm across, in small, leafy cymes. Sepals usually unequal, with marginal black glands. Petals pale yellow.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems stiffly erect, with 4 sharp ridges. Leaves oval, with numerous translucent glands and a few black glands. Flowers 12–15 mm across, numerous, in cymes. Sepals very acute. Petals slightly longer than the stamens, with a few black glands on the upper surface.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems erect with 2 (or sometimes 4) raised lines. Leaves 12–30 mm long, oval, obtuse, with few translucent glands or none, but usually with some black glands near the margin. Flowers 15–25 mm across, in cymes. Sepals obtuse. Petals bright yellow, slightly longer than the stamens, with black glands near the margin.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems slender, erect, up to 90 cm high, with two slightly raised lines. Leaves 12–20 mm long, oblong, obtuse, with numerous translucent glands, but without black glands. Flowers 15–25 mm across, in cymes. Sepals very acute. Petals bright yellow, usually with a few black glands near the margin, considerably longer than the stamens.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A delicate plant 10–25 cm high; stems slender, 4-angled, erect, smooth. Leaves narrowly oblong, obtuse, 7–15 mm long, with numerous translucent glands. Flowers rather few, 5–7 mm across. Sepals obtuse; petals narrow, pale yellow, with a crimson line on the lower side; stamens about 20.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 15–60 cm high, thin and wiry, usually hairy above. Leaves oblong-lanceolate, rather erect, 7–15 cm long. Flowers 17 mm across, rather few, in a lax, somewhat 1-sided raceme. Sepals deep pink or purplish-red; upper petals shorter and paler; labellum at least as long as sepals, white, veined with red and with yellow spots in the middle. Ovary slender, spindle-shaped, covered with short down.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 30–150 cm high, hairy above. Leaves broadly oval, dull green, strongly ribbed, flat, not in 2 ranks. Flowers 8–12 mm across, in a long 1-sided raceme. Sepals, blunt, dull green; petals shorter, blunt, tinged with pink; labellum reddish-pink, much shorter than sepals, with a sharp, reflexed tip. Ovary pear-shaped or cylindrical, more or less hairless.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to E. helleborine, differing in its smaller, folded, 2-ranked leaves, smaller, pendulous, green flowers, and hairless axis to the inflorescence.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 15–70 cm high, hairy, especially in the upper part. Leaves oval-oblong to lanceolate, concave and keeled, arranged in 2 ranks. Flowers 8–12 mm across, in a stiff, spike-like raceme. Sepals, petals and labellum dark red rarely straw-coloured; labellum shorter than the sepals. Ovary downy, pear-shaped, tapering to a very short pedicel.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem slender, 25–60 cm high, bearing rather numerous, erect, linear-oblong strap-shaped leaves. Flowers pure white, 12 mm long, rather erect, usually few, in a lax, graceful spike. Bracts very small, except for the lowest 1 or 2, which are often leafy. Sepals lanceolate; upper petals shorter and broader. Labellum constricted in the middle, as in Epipactis; upper half trough-shaped, with a yellow-orange spot near the base; lower half white with 3–7 orange ridges.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Whole plant, yellowish-brown without green pigment and growing as a saprophyte. Stem 25–35 cm high, arising from a tangled mass of stout, fleshy fibres. Leaves reduced to brown scales. Flowers 10 mm across, on short, twisted pedicels, in a long, cylindrical, spike-like raceme. Scented. Sepals and upper petals oval, entire; labellum twice as wide as long, with 2 spreading lobes.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 20–75 cm high; leaves 6–15 cm long, with sheathing bases, not cordate. Flowers green, rather small, numerous, in a long, slender, rather lax raceme. Sepals oval; upper petals linear-oblong, forming, with the sepals, a hood over the column. Labellum yellowish-green, 10–15 mm long, deeply divided into 2 linear, obtuse lobes.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to L. ovata, but shorter (3–20 cm high), with longer, often cordate leaves; much smaller flowers, reddish-brown, with the labellum no more than 5 mm long and deeply divided into 2 long and narrow, pointed lobes.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem slender, 7–35 cm high, leafless, but with a rosette of small, oval, pale bluish-green leaves beside it. Flowers in a single, spirally twisted row, forming a slender spike, scented. Sepals and petals free, the two lateral sepals pointing outwards, the upper forming a tube with the petals and labellum.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Leaves linear-lanceolate, erect, lower sheathing, upper bract-like. Flowers in 3 spirally twisted rows, forming a short dense spike; scented of hawthorn. Sepals and petals all united in the lower part and converging with lip to form a tube. Labellum white with green veins.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: 15–30 cm high; spike slender, lax and almost cylindrical; flowers white or cream, tinged with green, 6–12 mm  in length and 11–18 mm wide; pollinia vertical and parallel. Spur 13–20 mm long.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to P. bifolia but bigger in most of its parts; 27–60 cm high; spike broader and slightly pyramidal; flowers with the labellum longer and wider, 9–16 mm in length and 18–23 mm wide; pollinia leaning backwards and diverging downwards. Spur 18–30 mm long.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem leafy, 15–75 cm high. Leaves long and narrow, rather erect. Flowers numerous, 8 mm across, pinkish to reddish-purple, rarely white, very fragrant, in a long, moderately dense, cylindrical spike. Bracts narrow, longer than the ovary. Upper sepal and petals forming a hood; labellum broad, with 3 short, more or less equal lobes and a slender, pointed, slightly curved spur longer than the ovary. Ovary slender, stalkless, twisted and curved.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 10–40 cm high, rather stiff, bearing, near the base 3–4 oblong leaves. Flowers white, tinged green or yellowish-white; slightly fragrant, 3–4 mm across, in a dense, slightly 1-sided, cylindrical spike. Bracts as long as the ovary. Sepals and petals forming a loose hood over the longer labellum. Labellum deeply 3-lobed; mid-lobe, triangular and curved, longer than the tooth-like side lobes. Spur obtuse, thick and conical, one-third to half as long as ovary. Ovary stalkless, slightly twisted.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 8–25 cm high, with about 4 bluish-green oval-oblong leaves near the base. Flowers greenish, often edged or suffused with reddish-brown, 8 mm across, in a short, cylindrical spike. Bracts long and pointed. Sepals and upper petals forming a hood, the latter narrow and usually hidden. Labellum oblong, much longer than sepals, straight and hanging almost vertically, 3-lobed at the apex with the tooth-like middle lobe much smaller than the narrow, oblong laterals. Spur very short and obtuse, translucent. Ovary stalkless, twisted.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems solid, 15–60 cm high. Leaves lanceolate to linear-lanceolate usually less than 7 in number, usually 6–9 times as long as wide and heavily spotted with simple black spots, not as long as the flowering-spike. Spike pyramidal. Floral bracts about 15 × 2.5 mm. Flowers white sometimes tinged with pink. Labellum 6–14 mm wide, spotted or with spots and lines, deeply and unequally 3-lobed, the middle lobe the smallest. The lateral lobes often crenate. Spur delicate and thin, conical.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems solid, 15–60 cm high. Leaves oblong-lanceolate, spotted with transverse bars or merging spots, usually less than 7 in number, usually 4–6 times as long as wide, the lowest tongue-shaped, the second leaf the longest, the upper ones narrower, more pointed rarely exceeding the base of the flowering-spike. Floral bracts about 20 × 3.0 mm. Flowers pink, lilac, rarely pure white. Labellum flat, 5–12 mm wide, deeply and equally 3-lobed, with the middle lobe usually the longest; the lateral lobes rounded often crenate. Spur conical.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Rare plants growing in wood and heathland margins in western regions, more than 40 cm tall with more than 7 lightly spotted leaves, but with smaller spikes and flowers, belong to another distinct variety.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems hollow, 15–30 cm high. Leaves 3–8, 5–9 times as long as wide, usually unspotted, oblong-lanceolate, broadest near the base, tips hooded, longer than the flowering-spike. Floral bracts about 19–28 × 6 mm, the lowest exceeding the flowers. Flowers purple or pink, rarely white. Labellum more or less entire, sometimes with a small apical tooth, about 8 mm wide, side lobes usually reflexed. Spur tapering to a blunt point.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems somewhat hollow, 10–70 cm high. Leaves 3–11, 2–6 times as long as wide, lanceolate, (linear to linear-lanceolate in subsp. traunsteinerioides) often spotted transversely or with overlapping black spots, broadest near the middle, slightly exceeding the flowering-spike. Floral bracts about 1–4 × 0.8 mm. Flowers mauve to purple, lateral sepals marked with dots and lines. Labellum 3-lobed with the middle lobe by far the longest, rarely shallowly lobed.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 12–30 cm high. Leaves few, oblong, often with purplish-brown spots in parallel lines. Flowers 3–4 mm across, whitish or pink, never opening very fully, in a dense, narrow, cylindrical spike. Bracts shorter than ovary. Perianth greenish-white, sepals often streaked with a dull purplish-pink. Sepals and upper petals forming a hood. Labellum small, hanging, 3-lobed; middle lobe the largest; further divided at its tip into two to three lobes. Spur very short and blunt. Ovary twisted, stalkless.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 7–30 cm high. Leaves lanceolate, more or less basal, the upper sheathing and enclosing the stem. Flowers few, 15–20 mm across, in a short and rather lax cylindrical spike. Sepals purple or mauve, veined with green, all joining with the upper petals to form a hood. Labellum purple or mauve, broader than long, convex, 3-lobed with the mid-lobe equal to or shorter than the laterals. Spur horizontal to ascending, blunt and enlarged at its tip.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 12–60 cm high, stout. Leaves oblong, usually with rounded or oblong purple spots, the upper sheathing and enclosing the stem. Flowers 20 mm across, reddish-purple, sometimes pink, rarely white, in a long moderately dense, cylindrical spike, smelling strongly. Lateral sepals erect; upper one arched forward over the upper petals, its tip reflexed. Labellum broad, convex, 3-lobed paler at the base with a dark spotted area in the centre; middle lobe the longest, often notched. Spur stout, horizontal to ascending.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 25–45 cm high, slender or hairless. Leaves linear-lanceolate, mostly basal or nearly so, the lowest usually shrivelled at flowering. Flowers bright rose-pink or magenta, numerous, 6–8 mm across, with a foxy smell, in a short very dense, pyramidal spike which is later spherical. Lateral sepals lanceolate; the upper forming a loose hood with the petals. Labellum flat, with 2 upright pink plates at the base, divided into 3 blunt, sub-equal lobes. Spur very long and narrow, pointed, much longer than the ovary and extending to the opposite side of the flower spike. Ovary cylindrical, twisted, stalkless.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem slender, 20–60 cm high. Leaves oblong-lanceolate. Flowers about 15–20 mm across, 3–6 in a very lax spike. Sepals, large pale green, spreading, upper petals very narrow and antenna-like, purplish-brown. Labellum slightly convex, longer than the sepals, longer than wide, distinctly 3-lobed, the large middle lobe notched, purplish-brown with a blue patch in the centre.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar, but stem stouter, flowers somewhat larger, about 20–25 mm across with large, spreading, greenish-pink sepals and smaller, much-reduced lateral petals. Labellum broader than the sepals and almost as long, velvety-brown with yellow markings, (rarely greenish-yellow), 3-lobed, but reflexed and appearing entire from in front.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A very small plant, with a slender, angled stem 3–12 cm high, bulbous near the base, and with 2–5 small, concave, oval leaves, basal or nearly so, often fringed on the margins with minute bulbils from which new plants develop. Flowers yellowish-green, 4 mm across, in a rather dense, spike-like raceme; each flower is inverted, so that the triangular labellum, which is flanked by the paired sepals, is uppermost and the larger, unpaired sepal is lowermost. Perianth segments entire; petals, including labellum, shorter than the sepals. Spur absent.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Perennial, with a stout, woody rootstock. Stems prostrate, branched, stout, up to 40 cm long. Leaves 10–20 mm, narrowly oval, acute, pale bluish-green, often blackening on drying; margins rolled downwards. Stipules conspicuous, brown at the base, whitish above, with brown veins, at least as long as the internodes on the middle and upper parts of the stem. Flowers pink or white, solitary or 2–3 together in the leaf-axils. Nut 3.5–5 mm, glossy, equalling the perianth or slightly longer.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Annual; stems prostrate, rather woody, up to 100 cm long. Leaves widely spaced, lanceolate to oval, rather pale bluish-green and thick, with margins slightly rolled downwards. Stipules silvery, shorter than internodes except at the extreme tip of the stem. Flowers pink or greenish-white, in small axillary clusters. Nut 5–6 mm, dark brown, shiny, protruding from the perianth for about a third of its length.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Annual, with slender, branched leafy stems, erect or prostrate, up to 70 cm long. Larger leaves on the main stem (which often drop off early) up to 4 × 2 cm; those on the side-branches much smaller. Stipules silvery, not very conspicuous. Flowers almost stalkless, in small axillary clusters. Sepals green, edged with pink or white, broad and overlapping, shortly united at the base to form a tube about a quarter the length of the free lobes. Nut 3 mm, finely striated, not shiny, enclosed in the persistent calyx.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Like P. aviculare, but with stems always prostrate; leaves mostly 7–15 × 3–8 mm, all more or less equal in size; lobes of calyx narrower, 1.5–2 times as long as the tube; nut slightly smaller.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Annual; stems usually straggling or nearly prostrate, but occasionally erect. Larger leaves 20–75 mm long, at least 5 times as long as wide, oblong-lanceolate, broadest near the base. Flowers in small, erect, slender, lax spikes. Sepals deep reddish-pink, without glands. Nut about 2 mm long, enclosed in the calyx, black, shiny.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Like P. minus, but stems usually more or less erect; leaves 3–4.5 times as long as wide, narrowly elliptic, broadest near the middle; sepals pale pink, usually with a few flat glands; nut about 3 mm long.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Annual; stems usually erect but sometimes straggling and nearly prostrate, up to 50 cm high. Leaves 7–10 cm long, oval-lanceolate, very shortly stalked, downy beneath, often with a dark blotch on the upper side. Flowers in several compact, fairly stout, erect spikes. Sepals bright pink, rarely white, without glands. Stamens 5–8. Nut 3 mm, black, shiny, enclosed by calyx.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Like P. persicaria, but often larger and coarser, with leaves up to 15 cm long; flowers dingy pink or greenish-white; and with numerous raised, yellow glands on the peduncles and sometimes also on the pedicels and calyx
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Perennial, with long rhizome, often rooting at the nodes. Leaves sometimes floating, triangular-lanceolate, stalked, rounded or truncate at the base, up to 15 cm long. Flowers in erect, dense terminal spikes 2–4 cm long. Stamens 5; styles 2.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A nearly hairless perennial with short, stout rhizome. Lower leaves up to 15 cm, broadly oval, obtuse, long-stalked, with stalks broadly winged in upper part; upper leaves much smaller, triangular, with stalks sheathing the stem. Flowers in a dense, stout, terminal spike, bright pink. Stamens 8; styles 3. Nut 5 mm, brown.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Perennial, with short, compact stock. Stems erect, unbranched, up to 25 cm. Leaves oblong to linear-lanceolate, the lower ones stalked. Flowers in a slender, terminal spike, in the lower part of which the flowers are replaced by brown or purple bulbils, from which leaf-rudiments sometimes protrude. Calyx white. Stamens 8; styles 3. Nut rarely, if ever, developed.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Perennial, with erect stems up to 100 cm high and shortly creeping rhizome, forming dense clumps. Leaves oval, acute, the lower stalked, 15–20 cm long, the upper smaller, clasping the stem. Flowers crimson, in dense, cylindrical, terminal spikes. Stamens 8; styles 3.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Perennial with creeping rhizome and stout, erect stems up to 120 cm high, forming extensive clumps. Leaves oval-lanceolate, acute, shortly stalked, up to 25 cm long. Flowers white, in a diffuse, freely branched leafy panicle. Sepals free.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A downy perennial, spreading by stolons to form small clumps. Leaves oval, pointed, 7–10 cm long, shortly stalked; hairs whitish on the upper surface, usually buff beneath; mid-rib red. Flowers stalkless, in short spikes which are grouped into small, compact, usually leafy panicles. Calyx bell-shaped, with tube rather longer than the lobes, white in lower part, variably flushed with bright pink on the lobes. Stamens 8; styles 3.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A twining annual, with slender, angular stems up to 80 cm long. Leaves triangular-sagittate, pointed, stalked; stalks and lower part of blade rough with very short, stiff hairs. Flowers greenish-white or pink, in slender axillary spikes. Sepals 5, the 3 outer larger and keeled. Stamens 8. Fruit 4 mm long, dull black, minutely pitted.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems 150–200 cm high. Leaves mostly 8–10 cm long, broadly oval, with truncate base, narrowed suddenly at the tip to a slender point. Plants imperfectly dioecious (almost always female) in long, diffuse, lax panicles. Sepals 5, free, white; styles 3.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Like R. japonica, but with stouter stems up to 3 m high; leaves cordate at the base and rounded or gradually narrowed at the tip, usually 12–18 cm long; flowers yellowish-green, in fairly compact panicles, usually shorter than or equalling the adjacent leaf-stalk. Plants imperfectly dioecious.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A small, hairless perennial. Leaves nearly all basal, round or kidney-shaped with wavy margins, long-stalked, with acid taste. Flowers greenish, in a terminal panicle. Sepals 4, the two inner enlarging in fruit. Sepals 6; stigmas 2, feathery. Fruit flat, broadly winged.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems 7–30 cm high, erect from a slender, creeping rhizome. Leaves up to 4 cm long, hastate, with two divergent, acute basal lobes, acid to the taste. Dioecious. Flowers in slender, interrupted panicles. Inner sepals only slightly enlarged in fruit, shorter than the nut.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems erect, 35–80 cm high, sparingly branched. Leaves 3–12 cm long, with two basal lobes parallel to the stalk, acid to the taste. Dioecious. Flowers in usually fairly dense panicles. Fruiting sepals red, strongly keeled, 3–4 mm long, enclosing the narrow nut.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems stout, 100–180 cm high, with long, erect branches. Leaves lanceolate, tapered at both ends, 40–65 cm long; margin flat or very finely waved. Panicle large, fairly dense, somewhat leafy at the base. Fruiting sepals triangular, 6–7 mm long, each with an oblong tubercle.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems 50–200 cm high, with short, sub-erect branches. Leaves narrowly lanceolate; margins usually strongly wavy. Panicle rather dense, leafy at the base. Fruiting sepals 4–5 mm, broadly oval, usually all with a tubercle, but often one larger than the other two.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Rather slender; stem 60–80 cm high, branched from the base. Leaves oblong-lanceolate, untoothed, with slightly wavy margin. Panicle slender and sparse, with whorls of flowers clearly separated; all its branches leafy in the lower half. Fruiting sepals oblong, untoothed, 2.5–3 mm long, each with a well-developed tubercle.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Like R. conglomeratus, but with the panicle-branches leafless except at the extreme base, and only one of the fruiting sepals with a well-developed tubercle.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems somewhat straggling, up to 40 cm long. Leaves oval-oblong, many of them narrowed in the middle, so as to be violin-shaped. Panicle diffuse, with slender branches diverging almost at right angles from the main axis, furnished with small bracts and with the whorls of flowers well separated. Fruiting sepals 4–5 mm, with stout marginal teeth, and all three with tubercles, though often one is larger than the other two.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem stout, 50–120 cm high, with sub-erect branches. Leaves large, broadly oblong, slightly crenate, truncate or cordate at the base. Panicle leafless, dense, with stiff, erect branches. Fruiting sepals 5–6 mm long, toothed at least at the base, one with a large tubercle, the other two with smaller ones.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem erect, 40–70 cm high. Leaves linear-lanceolate, 5–15 cm long. Panicle freely branches, leafy throughout; whorls of numerous flowers often widely spaced below but compacted above. Fruiting sepals 2–3 mm, with long, slender, flexible marginal teeth, giving the panicle a shaggy appearance. The whole plant turns yellow at fruiting time.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Leaves numerous, narrowly linear, in a dense basal tuft. Peduncles unbranched, 6–20 cm high, usually hairy, with a single, tightly packed head of bright pink, papery flowers. Each head surrounded by a series of bracts; the outer largely green, the inner membranous; bracts continued down the peduncle as a sheath. Calyx papery, with fine teeth.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Leaves 5–25 cm long, distinctly stalked, with one obvious main vein. Flowering stems 10–30 cm high; usually bumpy to the touch; inflorescence open and the lower spikelets well separated. Calyx greenish-purple, with 5 principal, acute, finely toothed lobes alternating with 5 very much smaller lobes. Corolla bluish-mauve.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Like L. humile but generally smaller; with smaller leaves which have more than one obvious main vein and stems usually smooth (though sometimes slightly rough to the touch at the base), with branches in the upper part of the plant only and the calyx whitish with the ribs forming red stripes. An apomictic species.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Like L. procerum but with rough stems and branches in both the lower and upper parts of the plant and often with paler bluish-green leaves.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems tough, up to 80 cm high. Basal leaves with a broadish terminal lobe and 2–4 similar lateral lobes, all conspicuously and irregularly toothed; stem-leaves similar but smaller and with fewer segments. Flowers about 4 mm across. Fruits hairless when young, distinctly hairy on maturity, up to 18 mm long, pressed against the stem, in a long, slender raceme.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Often unbranched, hairy, up to 100 cm high. Basal leaves with a large hastate terminal lobe and 1–4 pairs of lateral lobes; stem-leaves similar but often with no lateral segments, or only 1 pair of lateral, finely divided, linear segments. Flowers about 8 mm across. Fruits hairy when young, up to 90 mm long, usually diverging, sometimes considerably, from the stem.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Much branched, sparsely hairy, up to 50 cm high. Basal leaves deeply divided with a smallish terminal lobe and 2–6 lateral paired lobes; stem-leaves with a hastate terminal lobe and up to 3 lateral lobes. Flowers about 5 mm across. Fruits hairless when young, up to 50 mm long, usually diverging slightly from the stem, the upper overtopping the flowers
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Much branched, sparsely hairy, up to 50 cm high. Basal leaves deeply divided with a smallish terminal lobe and 2–6 lateral paired lobes; stem-leaves with a hastate terminal lobe and up to 3 lateral lobes. Flowers about 5 mm across. Fruits hairless when young, up to 50 mm long, usually diverging slightly from the stem, the upper overtopping the flowers.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A rather delicate annual, 30–80 cm high, covered with soft, whitish down. Leaves finely divided, usually pinnate with deeply pinnately-lobed leaflets, the segments short and linear. Flowers very small, yellow, about 2 mm across, in long racemes; petals barely as long as sepals. Fruits hairless, somewhat beaded, up to 25 mm long, the pedicel spreading, the fruit-body slightly curved and fairly erect.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A nearly hairless, little branched biennial up to 120 cm high. Leaves mostly stalked, large, round or heart-shaped, with blunt teeth, smelling of garlic when crushed. Flowers white, 5 mm across. Fruits 30–60 mm long, somewhat spreading and beaded.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A slender, branching annual, 8–25 cm high. Leaves mostly basal, stalkless, oblong, coarsely toothed. Flowers white, very small, 2–3 mm across. Fruits cylindrical, slender, 10–20 mm long, spreading.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A stiff erect annual, 20–50 cm high covered with minute whitish hairs. Leaves green, lanceolate, entire or weakly toothed. Flowers small, yellow, 4–5 mm across. Fruits spreading, usually upcurved, 4-angled, slender, about 25 mm long; style short, evident.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Hairless or slightly hoary perennial, with bushy, rather woody stems 20–50 cm high. Leaves lanceolate, pointed, entire. Flowers large, yellow or orange, about 25 mm across, fragrant. Fruits somewhat flattened, upright, about 40 mm long; style bilobed, relatively long.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A coarse, hairy, erect biennial 60–100 cm high. Leaves large, broadly lanceolate, toothed, shortly stalked. Flowers 15–20 mm across, usually violet, sometimes pale pink, rarely whitish, fragrant at night. Fruits elongated, cylindrical, beaded, 50–100 mm long; style relatively long.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect biennial, hoary with short white down, 50–100 cm high. Stems tough at the base. Leaves narrow, fleshy, the lower ones pinnately lobed or with sinuate teeth. Flowers, large, lilac, about 18–20 mm across. Fruits long, cylindrical, somewhat spreading, 100–120 cm long; style indistinct, with 2 small lobes.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Erect, 30–60 cm high. Lower leaves pinnate, the terminal segment much longer and broader than the rest; upper ones toothed but usually not divided. Flowers bright yellow, in dense racemes, about 3 mm across. Fruits 4-angled, 15–30 mm long, ascending, with a relatively long, slender style [Fig. 82c].
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Very variable in habit, 30–90 cm high. All leaves pinnate with a large terminal lobe. Flowers in open racemes, about 5–7 mm across. Fruits 4-angled, sometimes rounded, 30–60 mm long, with a stout style [Fig. 82d].
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to B. verna but with flowers only about 3 mm across and fruits less than 30 mm long.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 60–120 cm high. Leaves variable, pinnately lobed, toothed or almost entire, the upper usually so. Flowers about 4 mm across, petals longer than sepals. Fruits very small, ovoid or nearly globular, about 6 mm long, widely spreading.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem creeping at the base; flowering branches erect, 30–60 cm high. Leaves pinnate, with lanceolate, toothed leaflets [Fig. 82e]. Flowers about 4–5 mm across; petals longer than sepals. Fruits narrow, cylindrical, about 10–18 mm long, upright [Fig. 82e].
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 15–40 cm, more or less erect, often bronze coloured. Leaves pinnately lobed with toothed segments [Fig. 82g]. Flowers about 3–5 mm across. Fruit oblong-ovoid, not more than twice as long as its pedicel, widely spreading 5–10 mm long [Fig. 82g].
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to R. palustris but more prostrate, stems not bronze coloured, with sepals and petals only 1–1.5 mm long and fruits more than twice as long as their pedicels.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless perennial up to 150 cm high, with large, stalked, oval-oblong, crenate or serrate leaves, and a large panicle of white flowers 8–10 mm across. Fruits not ripening to produce seed in this country.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Usually green in winter. Stem branched, stout but weak, partly floating or creeping. Leaves pinnate with oval leaflets. Flowers about 6 mm across. Fruits cylindrical oblong, 12–18 mm × 3–4 mm; seeds numerous, in 2 rows in each cell, coarsely reticulate with no more than 12 depressions across their width [Fig. 82h].
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Very like N. officinale, but with a fruit 18–25 × 2 mm, and with the seeds arranged more or less in a single row in the fruit, each finely reticulate with more than 12 depressions across their width [Fig. 82i].
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: The hybrid between N. officinale and N. microphyllum is often purplish-brown in winter and has fruits which are short, but narrow, with, at most, 3 well-formed seeds in each side (other malformed seeds may be present). The normal seeds have 10–14 depressions across their width [Fig. 82j].
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless perennial with weak stems, creeping at the base, 30–60 cm high. Leaflets all oval, slightly toothed. Flowers 12–14 mm across, pure or creamy white. Fruits with a fairly long style. Anthers violet.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A very variable, hairless perennial up to 60 cm high. Leaflets entire or bluntly toothed, those of the basal leaves round or oval, those of the stem-leaves narrowly lanceolate. Flowers 15–20 mm across, mauve or almost white; anthers yellow. Fruit with a short or longish style.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Annual, biennial or perennial, 12–30 cm high. Stem wavy, hairy at base. Leaves mostly basal; leaflets round, entire or toothed. Flowers very small, white, about 3–4 mm across; stamens 6. Fruits not overtopping the younger flowers; style short.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to C. flexuosa, but annual, shorter, with a straighter, hairless stem, 4 stamens and fruits which overtop the younger flowers.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Biennial to 80 cm. Stem erect, slightly wavy near the top. Leaves finely pinnate, with narrowly oval or lanceolate segments; the base strongly clasping with 2 sharply pointed auricles. Flowers sometimes 2 mm or less across. Fruits with a fairly long style.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A small, slightly hairy perennial, with mainly basal more or less pinnately-lobed leaves. Stem-leaves few, nearly entire, shortly stalked. Flowering stems 8–25 cm high; flowers white, about 7 mm across, sometimes more. Fruit slender, 15–30 mm long.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairy, stiffly erect biennial, 20–35 cm high. Basal leaves undivided, slightly toothed, in a loose rosette. Stem-leaves many, stalkless, usually clasping the stem with short basal lobes. Flowers small, white. Fruits long and slender, very erect and crowded.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect perennial, 15–30 cm high, covered with whitish hairs. Leaves small, stalkless, oblong, toothed; many of them basal, forming a rosette, but also several on the stem, not clasping it. Flowers small, white, 3–4 mm across; petals very slightly notched at the apex. Fruits erect, often twisted when mature.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Annual, up to 40 cm high, hairy but not whitish. Leaves oval, toothed, clasping the stem. Flowers and fruits similar to D. incana but the petals are not notched and the fruits are spreading.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Up to 15 cm high. Leaves with obvious petioles; leaves and flowering stems with a light covering of star-shaped hairs, green. Petals usually bifid for half–three-quarters of their length [Fig. 82k]. Seeds at least 0.5 mm long.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to E. verna, differing in the short petioles, greyish leaves, densely covered with star-shaped hairs, petals bifid for half of their length at most [Fig. 82l] and seeds less than 0.5 mm long.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Also similar to E. verna, differing in the very sparsely hairy leaves and petals bifid for half of their length at most [Fig. 82m].
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A small, erect annual. Leaves all stalked, slightly fleshy, the basal rounded to triangular, the uppermost ivy-shaped. Flowers small, in short racemes, about 4–5 mm across; petals usually mauve, sometimes white, no more than 4 mm long. Fruit ovoid, often narrowed at both ends.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A robust biennial with spreading stems and fleshy leaves; the basal ones large, entire, broadly triangular or kidney-shaped, on long stalks, the upper ones toothed, stalkless, and clasping the stem. Flowers about 8 mm across, in crowded racemes; petals 4–5 mm long, white. Fruit nearly globular.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Annual, rarely biennial, with more or less erect stems up to 30 cm high. Basal leaves elliptic-lanceolate, tapering gradually to a long stalk. Flowers about 8 mm across; petals 5–6 mm long, white. Fruit, flattened, ovoid to elliptical.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A rather slender, branched, hairy annual, 10–40 cm high. Basal leaves in a loose rosette, pinnately lobed or almost entire; upper leaves entire or slightly toothed, clasping the stem. Flowers very small, less than 2 mm across, white. Fruits flat, triangular to heart-shaped, 6–8 mm long.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A delicate, hairless annual with numerous unbranched flowering stems 5–15 cm high, arising from a rosette of small pinnately-lobed leaves. Flowers very small, 2.5 mm across, white, in racemes slightly less than half the height of the plant. Fruits flattened, nearly as broad as long, with an apical notch, spreading on longish pedicels.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, hairless, annual, 25–60 cm high. Leaves oblong, slightly toothed or lobed, the upper ones stalkless and clasping the stem with acute, rather divergent auricles. Flowers white, 6 mm across, or less. Fruits round and flat, 12–18 mm across, including the broad wing, deeply notched at the top.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Perennial, usually covered with white down; stems 15–40 cm high, branched from the base. Leaves lanceolate, entire or slightly toothed, stalkless and clasping the stem. Flowers 3 mm across, in very crowded racemes. Anthers violet. Fruit oblong, longer than broad, its upper part consisting of a flattened wing; style projecting from the shallow apical notch.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to L. heterophyllum but annual or biennial, usually with an unbranched stem; flowers smaller, in longer, looser racemes; anthers yellow and fruits rough and scaly.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems 50–100 cm high, arising from a creeping rhizome. Leaves large, lanceolate, stalked, slightly toothed. Flowers very numerous and crowded, about 3 mm across. Fruit nearly globular, not winged; style stout, short.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, perennial, 20–60 cm high. Leaves broadly elliptic; stem-leaves stalkless and clasping the stem with 2 large auricles. Flowers white, small, about 2 mm across. Fruits heart-shaped and flat, 4 mm across, un-winged, without an apical notch; style long and prominent.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Hairless, with numerous branched stems. Leaves fairly finely divided, with narrow segments. Flowers 2–3 mm across, in stalkless axillary clusters which lengthen into racemes in fruit; petals 1–1.5 mm; all stamens with anthers. Fruit 4 mm across, with an apical notch, deeply ridged and wrinkled.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to C. squamatus in habit, but usually hairy and with finer leaf segments. Flowers about 1 mm across, in regular, fairly compact racemes; petals minute or absent; only 2 stamens with anthers. Fruit 2–3 mm across, rounded or pointed at the top, its surface slightly rough.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A dwarf annual, 3–8 cm high, usually submerged. Leaves all basal, solid, slender, cylindrical, gradually tapering to a fine point, 12–25 mm long. Flowers white, minute, in a short, open raceme. Fruit ovoid, 3–4 mm long.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A small annual, with several stems 15–40 cm high. Leaves mostly basal, somewhat pinnately lobed but not deeply divided, with an unpleasant smell. Flowers yellow, 8–10 mm across, rather few, in loose racemes. Fruits spreading, hairless, slender, cylindrical, with a very short, evident style.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: 30–100 cm high. Lower leaves lyrate, hairless or with a few stiff hairs; upper leaves clasping the stem with broad, rounded auricles. Flowers about 17 mm across, usually shorter than the buds [Fig. 82o]. Fruits spreading, with a long, thin beak.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to B. napus, but the rosette leaves are usually green, the flowers smaller, usually overtopping the buds [Fig. 82p] and 9–13 mm across.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to B. napus but taller and with the upper leaves stalked and not clasping the stem. Flowers about 9–13 mm across. Fruits erect, pressed close to the stem, 10–18 mm long, with a short, slender beak.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: 30–70 cm high, with sparse, stiff hairs. Upper leaves stalkless, usually pinnately lobed or deeply toothed. Flowers 12–18 mm across, bright yellow. Fruits spreading, hairless or with stiff hairs pointing downwards, 25–50 mm long, including the conical beak which makes up about a third to a half of the total length, slightly beaded.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to S. arvensis, but slightly taller, the upper leaves usually stalked and more deeply divided, and the fruits covered with stiff, spreading, white hairs and ending in a flattened beak at least as long as the rest of the fruit.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Annual, hairy at the base, up to 150 cm high. Lower leaves pinnate; upper undivided, usually toothed. Flowers bright yellow, 7–9 mm across, in long racemes. Fruits cylindrical, with the beak containing a single seed, appressed [Fig. 82b].
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A bushy, hairless annual with spreading branches up to 40 cm long. Leaves few, fleshy, oblong, pinnately lobed. Flowers pale mauve or white, 12–15 mm across. Fruit 15–25 mm long, indehiscent, spindle-shaped, separating when ripe into two 1-seeded portions, of which the lower is the smaller and sometimes sterile.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A bushy annual; the upper parts hairless; lower parts with a scattering of coarse, spreading hairs. Leaves mainly basal in a rosette; rosette leaves lyrate; stem-leaves more or less stalkless and weakly toothed or lobed. Flowers about 7 mm across, in crowded, corymbose heads which elongate in fruit. Fruit beaked; the upper segment single seeded, strongly ribbed, with a prominent style; lower much smaller, sterile.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A stout, hairless perennial with large, pale bluish-green leaves (appearing somewhat waxy), irregularly pinnately lobed and waved at the margin. Flowers white, 10–15 mm across, in a large corymbose panicle. Fruit, globose, 1-seeded.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A coarse, somewhat hairy annual or biennial with large, lyrate, pinnate leaves. Flowers 18–25 mm across; petals white or yellow, often with violet veins. Fruit indehiscent, deeply constricted between the seeds and eventually breaking at the constrictions, with a long, pointed beak at the apex.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, usually unbranched, hairy annual up to 50 cm high. Leaves pinnate or pinnately lobed, the upper more divided. Flowers pale yellow, about 7 mm across, the lower in the axils of leaf-like bracts. Fruits shortly cylindrical, spreading with an evident style [Fig. 82q].
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, sparsely branched or unbranched, somewhat bristly hairy biennial, up to 1 m tall, distinctive due to its large almost circular, flattened fruits over 2 cm across which, on opening, reveal a persistent and shiny septum. Lower leaves long stalked, ovate to cordate and sharply toothed upper similar but stalkless. Flowers whitish to purple about 2.5–3 cm across.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A small, erect, hairy annual. Leaves oblong, hairy, mostly in a basal rosette usually dead at flowering time; a few opposite or alternate on the stem. Flowers 15–20 mm across, in small cymes, opening in the morning and falling in the afternoon. Petals pale yellow, usually with a dark red patch at the base. Stigma 3-lobed, almost stalkless.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Leaves 10–15 mm long, oblong; stipules 2–3 mm. Petals bright yellow. Style longer than ovary.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Leaves 5–8 mm long, oblong; stipules absent. Petals pale yellow. Style strongly curved, about as long as the ovary; stigma 3-lobed.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, hairy perennial; stems up to 75 cm high, often spotted with purple. Lower leaves round or kidney-shaped, not deeply lobed; middle and upper leaves palmately lobed almost to the base; lobes pinnately divided, with linear-oblong segments. Flowers 4–5 cm in diameter; petals notched, pink or white. Carpels hairy.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A straggling or nearly erect perennial, sparsely hairy. Leaves palmately lobed, about a third of the way to the base. Flowers numerous, in axillary clusters. Petals 15 mm, bright reddish-purple. Carpels usually hairless.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A small herb, usually annual. Stems up to 50 cm, more or less prostrate, downy. Leaves round to kidney-shaped, with 5–7 shallow, crenate lobes. Flowers numerous, in axillary clusters; petals 10 mm, pale lilac. Carpels downy.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A large, coarse, softly downy biennial; stems erect, up to 100 cm high, woody in the lower part, so that the plant is almost shrub-like. Leaves up to 10 cm across, nearly round, with usually 5 shallow, crenate lobes. Flowers in axillary or terminal panicles. Bracts of the epicalyx 3, united at the base, attached to the pedicel below the calyx, larger than the sepals and enlarging further in fruit. Sepals broadly triangular. Petals 10–15 mm, notched, overlapping, lilac-purple, with deep purple veins and base. Carpels downy.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, branched perennial, 50–100 cm high, covered with velvety down. Leaves broadly oval, often 3-lobed, toothed. Flowers in terminal racemes. Bracts of the epicalyx about 8, narrowly triangular, 5–7 mm long, free, inserted on the pedicel. Sepals ovate, pointed, slightly longer than the bracts. Petals 20 mm, scarcely notched, pale lilac-pink. Carpels downy.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem usually unbranched, erect and stiff, 50–100 cm high. Leaves narrowly lanceolate, entire. Pedicels about the same length as the yellowish-green flowers. Sepals usually 4; petals 4 or 5, the upper ones larger and deeply divided; stamens usually 20–25. Capsule nearly globular.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem usually branched, almost bushy, 30–50 cm high. Leaves ternately or pinnately divided, with linear segments. Pedicels longer than the yellowish-green flowers. Sepals and petals 6, sometimes 5; the upper petals variously divided. Stamens usually 15–20. Capsule oblong.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A large tree with spreading branches; bark smooth and grey at first, but scaling on old trunks. Winter buds greenish. Leaves 8–15 cm, about as broad as long, cordate at the base, with 5 acute, coarsely toothed lobes. Flowers in long, drooping, catkin-like panicles, appearing with or after the leaves. Wings of fruit diverging at rather more than a right angle..
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A large, broad-headed, deciduous tree with scaling bark. Buds large, very sticky in spring. Leaves opposite, palmate, with 5–7 leaflets up to 20 cm long. Leaf-scars with a characteristic pattern suggestive of a horse-shoe. Flowers in erect panicles. Calyx tubular, 5-lobed; petals 4 or 5 (if 5 then one is often much smaller), white with pink or yellow spots; stamens usually 7; ovary superior, 3-celled. Fruit a large, spiny, leathery capsule with 1–2 large brown seeds.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Very large tree to 40 m with orange or yellowish or greyish bark. Young leaves becoming orbicular; adult lanceolate. Flowers more or less stalkless. Fruit bowl-shaped with the valves clearly protruding from the top, 9–13 mm across.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Very large tree with whitish or greyish bark, up to 40 m high. Young and adult leaves lanceolate. Flowers more or less stalkless. Fruit bowl-shaped with the valves clearly protruding from the top, up to 9 mm across, smooth.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Moderately sized tree up to 12 m high with greyish or yellowish-brown bark. Young leaves orbicular; adult lanceolate. Flowers with distinct pedicels up to 4 mm long. Fruit urn-shaped with the valves hidden, 8–10 mm across.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Shrub or small tree up to 10 m tall with all leaves oval, sharply pointed, opposite; flowers with white or pale-pinkish, curved petals and a dark purple, globose berry.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A bushy shrub with brownish, eventually peeling bark and hairless, opposite, stalked, oval, toothed leaves; young stems often reddish. Flowers axillary, drooping, 3–4 cm across. Calyx crimson, 4-lobed; petals 4, deep purple, shorter than calyx lobes. Stamens 8, very long. Fruit a blackish, fleshy berry.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: 25–50 cm. high. Leaves usually slightly downy, not shining, somewhat triangular, very feebly toothed. Flowers 7–10 mm across; pedicels covered with glandular hairs. Fruit 2-seeded, drooping, covered with hooked bristles.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to C. lutetiana but with leaves slightly cordate, thinner, somewhat shining and more strongly toothed, with fruit nearly always not ripening.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems erect, 100–150 cm. Leaves hairy. Hairs on green parts of stem lacking red bulbous bases (though red-based on red parts of stem). Petals 1.5–3 cm. Sepals entirely green.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem erect, 40–150 cm, with long stiff hairs with red bulbous bases even on green parts of stem. Leaves hairy. Petals 3–5 cm. Sepals red-striped or entirely red.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Nearly hairless; stem unbranched 80–150 cm high. Leaves alternate, narrowly lanceolate, shortly stalked. Flowers deep purple-red, 25 mm across, in long terminal leafless racemes. Sepals almost linear and usually a deeper purple then the petals. Petals entire; upper two larger than the lower pair. Stigma 4-lobed.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems stout, 80–150 cm high, branched. Whole plant softly hairy with obviously long spreading hairs. Leaves mostly opposite, stalkless, almost clasping the stem, oblong-lanceolate, toothed. Flowers deep rose-pink, c. 20 mm across; stigma 4-lobed.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 30–90 cm high, more or less softly hairy with somewhat tangled, long spreading hairs. Leaves oblong-lanceolate, stalkless, slightly toothed or nearly entire, some alternate. Flowers pale pink, 8–10 mm across; stigma 4-lobed.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 15–60 cm high, creeping by stolons, slightly downy, the hairs mainly short and ± curled and appressed. Leaves hairless, oval-lanceolate, toothed, mostly opposite, at least the basal with a distinct stalk. Flowers pinkish mauve, 8 mm across; stigma 4-lobed. Buds slightly drooping.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem erect, branched, 30–60 cm high, with 2 or 4 longitudinal ridges running down from the bases of the leaves; short and leafy stolons formed above and below ground in summer. Leaves mostly opposite, stalkless, oblong-lanceolate, toothed, hairless. Buds erect. Flowers pale purplish-pink, 6–8 mm across, petals slightly lobed; stigma entire. Developing capsule with a few glandular hairs [Fig. 76c ].
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to E. obscurum, but stem cylindrical, without ridges; stolons at base long and thread-like, often underground; leaves linear-lanceolate and occasionally with a very short stalk; flowers only 5 mm across and buds drooping.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem slender, 30–60 cm high, slightly ridged, of varying density of hairiness, but with some glandular hairs. Leaves stalked, oval, toothed, nearly hairless; many of them alternate. Flowers very pale pink, 5 mm across. Stigma entire. Buds drooping.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem slender, decumbent, 5–15 cm, sparsely hairy with most hairs ± curled and appressed; leaves slightly toothed, shortly stalked and oval-lanceolate; flowers drooping bluish-red, 8 mm across. Stigma club-shaped.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 60–120 cm, stiff, with many sub-erect flowering branches and 4 longitudinal ridges (2 in lower part) running down from the leaves; hairless and reddish below, with both curled and ± appressed hairs and spreading glandular hairs above. Leaves mostly opposite, oblong-lanceolate with an acute tip, a subcordate shortly-stalked base and a hairless finely-toothed margin. Flowers 4–5 mm wide, numerous; petals pale pink with darker margins, deeply cleft. Stigma entire. Young capsule with both curled and ± appressed and glandular hairs [Fig. 76d ], hairless later, 4–6 cm. Seed with a pale translucent beak below the hair-tuft.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 20–50 cm stiff, with appressed, silky non-glandular hairs above, hairless below with 4 lines running down from the leaves, downy above with appressed hairs; forming almost stalkless leaf-rosettes in autumn. Leaves 4–6 cm × 6–9 mm, strap-shaped, blunt at tip, almost stalkless, decurrent, hairless. Flowers 6–8 mm, lilac-pink, slightly notched. Young capsule with short crisped hairs but lacking glandular hairs, 7–10 cm long when mature [Fig. 76e ].
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems slender, creeping. Leaves opposite, round, slightly toothed, 3–6 mm across, often reddish or purplish underneath. Flowers small, white or pale pink, erect on short stalks.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to E. brunnescens but with larger (4–9 mm) obviously toothed leaves.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A stiff, erect, usually shortly hairy perennial up to 1 m high. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3, stalkless, lanceolate, 5–10 cm long. Flowers in dense, reddish-purple whorls in terminal spikes. Calyx with twice as many teeth as petals, the narrowly triangular teeth alternating with the rounded. Petals usually 6. Stamens twice as many as petals of two distinct lengths in any one flower. Ovary deeply sunk in the calyx-tube but free from it.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A creeping, hairless annual, forming small tufts. Leaves opposite, oval, 10–15 mm long, stalked at the base. Flowers very small, stalkless, axillary and numerous. Calyx 12 toothed; the broadly teeth triangular alternating with the linear. Petals 6, small, purple, sometimes absent. Stamens 6. Top of ovary overtopping the calyx.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A delicate annual, with very slender, erect stems up to 15 cm high, usually forked above. Leaves 5–10 mm, narrowly oval, opposite. Flowers 6–8 mm across. Sepals narrow, acute; petals 4 mm × 2 mm, white.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Biennial, with erect, sparingly branched stems up to 60 cm high. Leaves alternate, linear-oblong, acute. Flowers 15–20 mm across. Sepals broad, mucronate. Petals pale blue.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Leaflets green. Flowers solitary, on long stalks, 15–20 mm across, white, veined with purple.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Plant creeping and rooting at the nodes. Leaflets often purple. Flowers 4–7 mm across, yellow, in umbels of about 6 flowers, umbels on longish stalks.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Plant more or less upright. Leaflets green. Flowers 5–9 mm across, yellow, in rather few-flowered umbels of no more than 5.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Plant more or less upright. Flowers 10–15 mm across, pink, in few- to many-flowered umbels, umbels on long stalks.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A deciduous shrub with green, 4-angled twigs. Leaves opposite, oval, acute, shortly stalked, entire or minutely toothed. Flowers 8–10 mm across, in small, axillary cymes. Sepals, petals and stamens 4. Petals free, pale green. Ovary 4-celled, superior, square in face-view. Fruit a somewhat fleshy 4-lobed capsule, bright pink, splitting to expose the orange arils, in each of which a seed is enclosed.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, hairless perennial, 15–40 cm high, with long-stalked, entire, heart-shaped basal leaves. Stem with a single stalkless leaf. Flowers 20–25 mm across, solitary. Sepals slightly united at the base. Petals free, white, with translucent veins, slightly notched at the tip. Stamens 5, alternating with 5 staminodes; these have a broad, white base, divided above into about 12 slender branches, each ending in a greenish-yellow gland. Ovary 1-celled; stigma 4-lobed, stalkless. Fruit a capsule.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.
